messages:
sam: FYI ran a quick nsys capture against the latest staging runtime and found a regression in kernel launch tail latency after the batching heuristic change. attaching trace link: https://perf.internal/trace/1791234567 :grimacing:
anya: ugh. which change exactly? the batching heuristic PR or the kv-cache refactor?
sam: looks correlated to batching heuristic PR (commit abc1f9e). timeline shows long gaps between cuLaunchKernel calls where previously we had continuous streaming. hot kernel is the attention fwd.
kevin: can you paste the nvprof/nsys snippet?
sam: ```
nsys stats --report gpusummary trace.qdrep
-- kernel: multi_head_attn_fwd
-- avg time (before): 0.74ms
-- avg time (after): 1.85ms
-- peak cuLaunchKernel wait: 2.3x
-- observed under batch size mix: many small seqs (1-8)
```
li: interesting — also seeing KV cache hit rate drop in telemetry for that rollout?
sam: yes. kv cache hit % for prefix reuse dropped from 98% to ~76% on sample prompt set. suspect batching merge changed request ordering, invalidating prefix keys.
perf-bot: New profile uploaded by sam: https://perf.internal/trace/1791234567 (size 43MB). Tags: nsys, nvprof, perf-regression
anya: steps to reproduce?
sam: quick repro: run loadgen with mix of seq lengths (1,2,4,8) with sticky sessions. command: ```./run_loadgen --model redwood-v1 --seq-mix small --sticky=true --concurrency=48 --runtime=staging```
sam: then capture: ```nsys profile -o out --trace=nvtx,cuda --sample=none ./run_loadgen ...```
kevin: ok, run bisect plan: is commit range known?
li: we narrowed to between abc1f9e and d4f2b22 (2 commits). could be batching PR plus an autoscale tweak.
sam: I ran a binary search locally across those two; d4f2b22 seems to be the culprit but we need full trace comparisons. plan: bisect with nsys snapshots on CI and diff kernel timelines.
anya: do we have a lightweight diff script?
kevin: I pushed a small tool `tools/trace_diff.py` on my branch. usage: ```python tools/trace_diff.py before.qdrep after.qdrep --kernels attention* --out report.html```
li: small note — when you compare, normalize for concurrency and device occupancy. the prior runs had smaller active warps because of changed batching. otherwise numbers lie.
sam: agreed. I captured perfetto flame of one run; here's the top region: ```
0.000 - 0.120s: io/recv (small)
0.121 - 0.140s: prefix_kv_lookup (was 0.006s before)
0.141 - 0.260s: multi_head_attn_fwd kernel (spikes, see gaps)
0.261 - 0.320s: cuStreamSynchronize waits
```
kevin: that prefix_kv_lookup jump explains cache drop. batching probably reorders requests causing misses or extra key evictions.
anya: immediate mitigation: revert batching heuristic in staging or force stable ordering for prefix requests. which is easier?
li: revert is fastest for rollout rollback. but long-term we should make batching heuristic preserve prefix continuity or tag requests with cache-group id.
sam: I'll open a hotfix PR to revert heuristics and add a config toggle. PR draft: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/4521
perf-bot: perf alert created: regression 1.85ms vs 0.74ms, impact on p99 latency +18%. Ticket: PERF-1129
kevin: can infra run the bisect job on the GPU fleet? cheaper to run CI bisect with `--min-reps 3` and automatic trace upload.
infra-bot: Scheduling bisect: running `git bisect run` across commits abc1f9e..d4f2b22 on fleet label=staging-gpu-small. will upload per-commit traces to https://perf.internal/bisect/1791234567/
li: when bisect completes, we should get before/after qdrep and nvprof. i'll automate the KV-cache lookup times extraction.
anya: thanks everyone. sam — please attach the initial two qdrep files to the PR and set rollback flag on deployment dashboard if we see customer impact. :thumbsup:
